shipped.kurz: The old decretals: Exiit qui seminat (1279) and Exivi de paradiso (1312)
shipped.warum: What the dispute was about, from Friedberg's Corpus iuris canonici, Latin with a working translation, in excerpts: Nicholas III declares renunciation of ownership 'not only individually but also in common' the way of Christ, explains Christ's purse as condescension to the weak, and distinguishes property, possession, usufruct, the right of using and the 'simple use of fact'; the Roman Church takes the ownership; no one may gloss it. Clement V at Vienne hears the Spirituals' list of the Community's excesses and rules on granaries and 'poor use'.

shipped.kurz: The pope's dossier: the decretals of John XXII
shipped.warum: Five decretals on 'the meaning of words', from Friedberg's Corpus iuris canonici, Latin with a working translation: obedience above poverty (1317); the question opened (1322); the Roman Church renounces its 'verbal, bare and enigmatic' ownership of the friars' goods, since no one can use an egg without owning it (1322); the assertion that Christ had nothing 'nor even in common' declared heretical (1323); the friars' 'key of knowledge' called a doctrine of the father of lies (1324).

shipped.kurz: The Book of Sentences: four Beguins handed to the secular arm (1322)
shipped.warum: Bernard Gui's general sermon at Toulouse, 12 September 1322, from the register of the inquisition printed by Limborch (1692), Latin read from the page with a working translation: Guillaume Ruffi, who asked how the Beguins burned at Narbonne had died; Pierre Dominici, who took off his crosses, called John XXII a heretic for allowing the friars granaries, and kept a litany of about seventy condemned; Pierre Hospitalis, for whom the pope had ceased to be pope; Pierre Guiraud, who would not swear to name his companions; and the sentences 'short of death', which meant death.

shipped.kurz: The order's chronicle: Perugia, the appeal, the flight (1322–1329)
shipped.warum: Nicholas Glassberger's chronicle, from the Analecta Franciscana (1887), Latin with a working translation: the letter of the general chapter of Perugia (4 June 1322) that Christ and the apostles had nothing 'individually and in common', signed by Michael of Cesena and his masters; Michael before the pope 'not as reverently as he ought'; Bonagratia's appeal and his year in a dark prison; the galley, the flight by night, the deposition at Bologna, the appeal nailed to the doors of Pisa, and the chapter of Paris that declared the pope 'had defined well'.

The general's own account, in the notarial instrument he had drawn up in secret in the Franciscan convent of Avignon, from Baluze-Mansi (1762), Latin read from the page with a working translation: summoned, sick, received 'peacefully and kindly'; then on 9 April called 'a supporter of heretics' for the Perugia letter; 'if it were heretical, Pope Nicholas would have been a heretic'; a pope who condemns Exiit condemns himself; the appeal made 'from a fear that can fall on a steadfast man'.

shipped.kurz: Dante, Paradiso XI: Francis and Lady Poverty
shipped.warum: The whole canto, in Moore's Oxford text (1904) and Longfellow's translation (1867): Thomas Aquinas tells the life of Francis as a marriage to Poverty, widowed eleven hundred years since she 'climbed the cross with Christ', and ends with the decline of his own Dominican order. Written in the years of the first phase of the dispute, before the pope's question of 1322.

Louis the Bavarian's appeal against 'John, who calls himself pope', in the first form drafted with Franciscans at his court, from Schwalm's MGH edition (1909–13): the king's charges, the chapter on the highest poverty (the stigmata as Christ's seal on the rule, 'which no leaden bull can overturn'; the key of knowledge that binds every later pope), and the appeal to a council in the words of Philip IV against Boniface VIII.

Ockham's answer from Munich to Quia vir reprobus, in Goldast's printing (1614), seven excerpts read from the page images with a working translation: the prologue that reports both sides and replies 'to nothing, since I do not know'; use of fact and the right of using, defined as a power one can defend in court, and the poor guests at a rich man's table; property as a power that came after the fall; Judas's purse; what a pope may and may not change; and the heretic who will not be corrected.

shipped.kurz: Bernard Gui's manual: the sect of the Beguins (c. 1323–1324)
shipped.warum: The inquisitor of Toulouse on the lay followers of Olivi, from his Practica in Douais's edition (1886), eleven excerpts read against the page images with a working translation: Olivi read in the vernacular in 'houses of poverty', the greeting 'Blessed be Jesus Christ', the articles on Christ's poverty and on a pope who allowed granaries and so ceased to be pope, the four friars of Marseille venerated as martyrs, the bones of the burned kept as relics, and the questions to put to a suspect.

The Spirituals' own history, by a man who stood before John XXII in 1317, from Ehrle's edition (1886), twelve excerpts read against the page images with a working translation: Olivi's violated grave, the audiences at Avignon ('Nolumus, nolumus'; 'ask them why they drove me out'; 'you wear five tunics'), the four burned at Marseille, Bonagratia as the Community's prosecutor, the question of 1321 and the verdict that the order now defended poverty 'by the same spirit' that had persecuted it, Ubertino made a monk, and Francis's habit in the form of a cross.

missing.warum: The author behind the Beguins, the Spirituals and the Perugia doctrine is present here only through others: the inquisitor, Clareno and the condemned. His questions on evangelical poverty and on 'poor use' and his postill on the Apocalypse are available in full only in modern editions still in copyright; the older extracts printed by Ehrle (1887) were not examined for this stage. A gap by necessity.

missing.kurz: Quia vir reprobus (16 November 1325), the bull itself
missing.warum: John XXII's long reply to Michael of Cesena, with the argument that Adam had property before the fall. It is public domain and printed in the Bullarium Franciscanum, but it is carried only through Ockham, who quotes it phrase by phrase (OND). A gap by choice.

missing.kurz: Michael of Cesena's appeal of Pisa, 'in majori forma' (1328)
missing.warum: The long appeal Michael renewed at Pisa, to the Church and a general council, with its articles against the pope; only the short appeal of Avignon is carried. A gap by choice, for length.
missing.quelle: Baluze, Miscellanea, ed. Mansi, III (Lucca 1762), pp. 246 ff.

missing.kurz: The Chronicle of the Twenty-Four Generals
missing.warum: The order's fourteenth-century chronicle, on which Glassberger draws. No scan of its edition could be used; the order's voice is carried through Glassberger, who copies it. A gap by necessity.

The other great theorist at Louis's court. He treats evangelical poverty at length in the second discourse (chapters 12–14), but as part of an argument against the temporal power of the clergy, not as a document of the dispute itself; he appears here on the timeline only. A gap by choice.
missing.quelle: Defensor pacis, ed. C. W. Previté-Orton (Cambridge 1928).

missing.kurz: Umberto Eco, Il nome della rosa (1980)
missing.warum: The novel that made the dispute famous is set in its last year, 1327. It is in copyright and is named, never quoted.
